body:
Fixes #1

Adds the medical speech research plan and a working browser experiment. The [case study](https://github.com/konard/medical-speech-to-text/blob/issue-1-362226f4199c/docs/case-studies/issue-1/README.md) maps all 22 requirements to implementation, sources, experiments and acceptance criteria.

- Compares 20 industry solution families and clinical workflow products using dated primary sources. Covers Australian AWS processing and storage, access checks, streaming latency, dataset governance, preprocessing, exact microphone configurations, multichannel experiments, clinical review, support and the training ladder through an independently trained network.
- [Speech Lab online demo](https://raw.githack.com/konard/medical-speech-to-text/issue-1-362226f4199c/examples/speech-lab/index.html) runs pinned Whisper tiny/base models locally. Load ten attributed public consultation clips or 1–20 files; references are optional. Results include actual text, WER/CER where references exist, word highlighting during playback, seeking, cancellation and JSON provenance export.
- Adds native JavaScript acceptance tests, a tested Links Notation provenance example, browser tests and a real-model CI job. Preserves the inherited APIs and acceptance assertions; includes one minor changeset.

To reproduce: `npm ci && npm test && npm run check`; then `npm ci --prefix examples/speech-lab`, `npm --prefix examples/speech-lab run build`, install Chromium with Playwright, and run the demo's `test:browser` and `test:model` scripts. The public sample generator verifies pinned source hashes and reproduces the crop frames.

Validation: full suites pass under Node (1041), Bun (1041) and Deno (1040, one inherited CLI symlink skip). Browser checks cover references, actual audio playback/seek highlighting, failure continuation, cancellation and export. Real model execution covers all ten clips plus a base-model recording without a reference. Lint, formatting, duplication, secrets, documentation, file limits, workflow policy and dependency audit checks are included. Fresh browser results are retained as CI artifacts.

The committed observed tiny run scores **27.9% WER / 17.7% CER** on 40.94 seconds from one mock consultation. It takes several seconds per clip; it establishes neither subsecond streaming nor clinical safety. Paid API entitlements, private clinical data, Australian infrastructure, physical hardware trials and training are fully specified research stages, with explicit prerequisites and exit criteria. The public demo downloads globally delivered assets and is intended for public or synthetic data; the case study specifies the restricted Australian deployment.

The public URL was verified from a fresh browser on 30 October 2026, including all ten clips, the unreferenced base result and word seeking/highlighting ([receipt](https://github.com/konard/medical-speech-to-text/blob/issue-1-362226f4199c/docs/case-studies/issue-1/data/online-verification.json)). If the host shows **External Content Notice**, select **Open the page**. Its empty acknowledgement POST occurs before recordings are selected; application/model requests remain GET/HEAD only.

Actual model output and active-word highlighting:

![Speech Lab actual model results](https://github.com/konard/medical-speech-to-text/blob/issue-1-362226f4199c/docs/screenshots/speech-lab/result.png?raw=true)

[Mobile verification screenshot](https://github.com/konard/medical-speech-to-text/blob/issue-1-362226f4199c/docs/screenshots/speech-lab/mobile.png?raw=true) · [Raw execution evidence and limitations](https://github.com/konard/medical-speech-to-text/blob/issue-1-362226f4199c/docs/case-studies/issue-1/verification.md)
